model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 40 to 65, with tick marks every 5 units. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 39% accuracy and plateaus around 44% as co-occurrence increases. The FT method (blue line with triangular markers) begins at about 40% and rises to approximately 47%. The IKE method (red line with triangular markers) starts at roughly 43% and increases to about 49%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at approximately 44% and reaches around 56%. The MEMIT method (purple line with diamond markers) starts at about 44% and climbs to approximately 55%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) shows the highest performance, starting at around 51% and increasing to approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods exhibit increasing accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers, with ROME consistently outperforming the others.
